title: kith-peer: Peer/deliver inbound handler
description:
What: Implement the Peer/deliver JMAP method handler in kith-peer — the inbound path that accepts a message from a peer mailbox, validates it, stores it, and emits a state-change push.

Algorithm:
1. Deserialize args (serde_json::Value) into PeerDeliverArgs struct: { accountId: String, message: { id: String, chatId: String, senderTailscaleUserId: String, body: String, bodyType: String, attachments: Vec, replyTo: Option<String>, sentAt: String } }
2. Acquire AppState lock briefly to get owner_id
3. Call check_sender(&caller.identity, &args.message.sender_tailscale_user_id) -> Err maps to JmapError::invalid_arguments("senderTailscaleUserId mismatch"); this MUST happen before any DB write
4. Validate args.message.body.len() <= 65536 bytes; return JmapError::request_too_large if exceeded
5. Validate args.message.body_type is "text/plain" or "text/markdown"; else JmapError::invalid_arguments
6. Validate args.message.id is valid ULID via ulid::Ulid::from_string; else JmapError::invalid_arguments
7. Compute expected_chat_id = kith_core::compute_chat_id(&[caller.identity.user_id, owner_id]); compare to args.message.chat_id; reject if mismatch
8. Acquire store lock; if replyTo is Some, call store.messages().get(&reply_to_id) -> verify exists and chat_id matches; else JmapError::invalid_arguments
9. Call store.messages().insert(id, chat_id, sender_user_id, body, body_type, Some(sent_at_peer), created_at_unix, &DeliveryState::Received, reply_to) -> propagate as JmapError::server_fail on Err
10. Call store.contacts().upsert(peer_user_id, login_name, node_name, display_name, now_unix) -> propagate as JmapError::server_fail on Err (auto-create contact here, not in separate bead)
11. Release store lock; return Ok(json!({ "accountId": "a-self", "accepted": true, "receivedAt": received_at_rfc3339 }))

Note: KITH-nu1 (auto-create Contact) is folded into step 10 above; KITH-nu1 bead closes as covered here.

Defensive rules:
- check_sender MUST be called before any DB write (step 3)
- chatId MUST be recomputed (step 7); never trust peer-supplied value
- replyTo MUST be validated in same chat before insert (step 8)
- node_name comes from caller.identity.node_name (WhoIs); NOT from request body
- Never log message body; log only message_id and chat_id
- Return JmapError on all validation failures; never unwrap() on args parsing

Agent team: Researcher R reads kith-core auth.rs, kith-store message.rs, kith-jmap Dispatcher pattern. Implementer I writes PeerDeliverArgs struct + DeliverHandler implementing JmapHandler. Tester T derives expected JSON from RFC 8620 §3 and kith protocol spec. Validator V runs cargo test --workspace + clippy.

Tests (T's independent oracle = RFC 8620 + kith-architecture.md spec):
- Happy path: valid Peer/deliver args -> Ok response with accepted=true and receivedAt set
- check_sender mismatch: senderTailscaleUserId != WhoIs user_id -> JmapError before any DB write; verify no message row created
- Bad chatId: chatId != compute_chat_id([sender, owner]) -> JmapError::invalid_arguments
- Body too large: body.len() > 65536 -> JmapError::request_too_large
- Invalid ULID: id="not-a-ulid" -> JmapError::invalid_arguments
- Invalid bodyType: bodyType="text/html" -> JmapError::invalid_arguments
- Bad replyTo: replyTo references non-existent message -> JmapError::invalid_arguments
